faq.a: Increasing pressure compresses the ascending RAS, reducing cortical arousal and causing progressive loss of consciousness.
faq.q: Why does raised intracranial pressure affect consciousness?

faq.a: Yes; diffuse edema or metabolic encephalopathy may not be visible, so rely on clinical GCS and treat the cause.
faq.q: Can a patient with a normal CT still have a dangerous RAS problem?

faq.q: When is intubation mandatory in altered consciousness?

exam: A 7‑year‑old with cerebral malaria is drowsy, GCS 10 – what is the next immediate step? — Secure airway (intubate) if GCS ≤8 or deteriorates; otherwise give IV artesunate and monitor for ICP.

A patient presents with sepsis and GCS 13 – how do you differentiate delirium from RAS compression? — Look for focal neurological signs, papilledema, or imaging; delirium shows fluctuating attention without structural lesions.

Why is mannitol preferred over steroids for acute raised ICP in low‑resource settings? — Mannitol reduces cerebral water content quickly; steroids have no benefit in traumatic or infectious edema and may worsen infection.
What bedside sign suggests impending brain herniation? — Fixed, dilated pupil on the side of a mass lesion indicates uncal herniation.
How would you manage hypoglycaemia causing reduced consciousness when glucose testing is unavailable? — Give 50 % dextrose IV empirically; reassess mental status within minutes.
A patient on anticholinergic overdose is obtunded – why avoid physostigmine in malaria‑endemic areas? — Physostigmine can precipitate seizures in cerebral malaria; supportive care is safer.
Explain why a normal CT does not rule out RAS dysfunction in TB meningitis. — Early meningitis may show only subtle basal enhancement; clinical signs and CSF analysis are essential.
What is the significance of a Cushing’s triad in a comatose patient? — It indicates raised ICP and impending herniation; urgent measures to lower pressure are required.

ai.subject: Physiology
ai.summary: The reticular activating system (RAS) is a brainstem network that regulates arousal and consciousness. Disruption causes altered mental status, from lethargy to coma, especially with raised intracranial pressure. Understanding its function guides bedside assessment and emergency management.

b: Fluctuating attention suggests delirium from RAS disruption
sections.p: The RAS is a diffuse set of neurons in the brainstem that project to the thalamus and cortex, maintaining wakefulness and attention. Clinically it is diagnosed by the level of consciousness using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS).

sections.p: Altered consciousness is staged by GCS: 13‑15 mild, 9‑12 moderate, ≤8 severe (coma). In low‑resource settings, bedside GCS is the primary tool.
